title: Detect long-running outbound tasks on network threads

timeline.message:
Detect long-running outbound tasks on network threads

Extends the mechanism introduced in #109204 to cover slow-running
outbound tasks too.

Closes #108710
Closes ES-8625
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.body: I think you can stop activity inside doFlush, or wrap doFlush, something like `trackingDoFlush`.
Write path might include compression and encryption, does it count as non-network stuff?

If compression/encryption blocks the network thread for several seconds then yes absolutely we care about that.

Also answering an earlier question:

> Would it be easier to track activity on the thread-pool itself?

Not obviously, although if you have an idea for how to detect this more generally then I'd love to hear it.

> Not obviously, although if you have an idea for how to detect this more generally then I'd love to hear it.

I think one of the options is to wrap EventExecutor with time tracking and custom EventExecutorChooserFactory. Haven't tried my self, thats why removed that comment. https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/6905#issuecomment-999604847
